skill.name: set-up-lightspeed-google-ads-returning-customer-bidding
skill.description: Use Product Metrics to set up returning customer bidding for Lightspeed eCom in Google Ads. Verify repeat-order conversions and choose whether a retention campaign optimizes for revenue or profit.
skill.summary: Set up Google Ads bidding on revenue or profit from Lightspeed repeat orders.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: The audit dismissed 63 static matches and retained one for an unpinned installer. The workflow also permits assistant handling of credentials, can extend onboarding to unrelated ad channels, and can substitute live documentation for reviewed files. No evidence of prompt injection or credential exfiltration was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: The optional install command does not pin the installer package or skill revision.
remediation.suggestion: Publish a verified installer version and immutable skill revision. Require separate user approval before running an install command.

remediation.issue: The main workflow permits the assistant to accept and pass credentials despite the Lightspeed reference directing users to keep them out of chat.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the credential exception. Route key entry through the authenticated Product Metrics app, then verify connection status without reading the credentials.

remediation.issue: The fallback checklist can lead users to connect ad channels outside the requested Google Ads setup.
remediation.suggestion: Limit this workflow to the named workspace, store, and Google Ads client account. Require separate authorization before starting integrations or data sharing for other channels.

remediation.issue: The workflow can substitute live vendor Markdown for the bundled references without verifying its revision.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the reviewed references or verify their hashes against the audited release. Treat live pages as informational and stop if required instructions cannot be verified.

semantic_findings.title: Assistant workflow can expose Lightspeed API credentials
semantic_findings.description: The main rule permits requesting the Lightspeed API key and secret and passing them to a command. The reference says to enter them only in the app and keep them out of chat. Assistant input or command arguments could expose the credentials in transcripts, tooling logs, or process listings. The requested permissions include customer and order reads and write access to Settings and Tracking.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The two credential instructions conflict, and the read and write permissions are documented. No credential collection or leak was observed.

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The named fallback explicitly lists all three channels without a Google Ads-only condition. Additional connections still require user action.

content.user_title: Set Up Returning Customer Bidding for Lightspeed
content.value_statement: A Google Ads retention campaign can optimize for first purchases unless its conversion goal distinguishes repeat orders. This skill uses Product Metrics to verify Lightspeed repeat-order conversions and guides you through choosing a revenue or profit goal.
actual_capabilities: Reads setup status through the Product Metrics CLI or MCP and identifies unfinished steps.
Guides the Lightspeed C-Series and Google Ads tracking setup, including consent configuration.
Checks recent Lightspeed orders and reports whether customers are new, returning, or unknown.
Explains which Google Ads action represents repeat-order revenue and which represents repeat-order profit.
Guides a paid repeat test order and checks whether the selected conversion action is primary after the user changes it.
limitations: Requires Lightspeed eCom C-Series on the EU or US cluster, Product Metrics Pro, and a compatible Cloudflare setup.
Requires a connected Google Ads client account with linked Merchant Center. Account approvals and primary goal changes are manual.
Profit conversions need complete order costs and active additional costs. Unpaid orders and orders without a matched customer do not generate repeat-order conversions.
This workflow does not configure new-customer or lifetime-value bidding. It does not guarantee that a campaign will reach its target ROAS.

use_cases.title: Check repeat-order tracking
use_cases.description: Review recent orders to see which qualify as repeat purchases before changing campaign settings.

use_cases.title: Configure a retention campaign goal
use_cases.description: Choose a revenue or profit conversion for one campaign and verify the goal after changing it in Google Ads.

use_cases.title: Diagnose a missing conversion
use_cases.description: Use a paid repeat test order to check customer matching, consent settings, and conversion readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Check prerequisites
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: review setup without changing accounts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check setup for my Lightspeed store [store] and Google Ads client account [account]. Tell me which connections are ready and what I still need to do. Do not make changes.

prompt_templates.title: Review recent repeat orders
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: verify how the store classifies orders.
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize the last 20 paid orders in [store] by new, returning, or unknown customer. Explain why any orders could not be classified. Leave out customer identifiers.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a campaign conversion goal
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare a manual goal change for one campaign.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare revenue and profit goals for [campaign]. Check whether profit data is ready and show me how to switch the goal in Google Ads. Leave other campaigns unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a test order and campaign goal
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: validate tracking after a manual goal change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Read back the conversion goal for [campaign] after my change. Check whether paid test order [order ID] was classified as returning. List any consent, cost, or delivery checks I still need to complete. Do not make changes.

output_examples.input: Is my retention campaign ready to bid on repeat-order profit?
output: Google Ads tracking is ready, and both returning-customer actions are secondary.
Additional costs are not active, so the profit action is not ready for bidding.
Activate additional costs and verify a paid repeat order before changing the campaign goal.

output_examples.input: Check my paid test order and confirm the goal I selected.
output: Product Metrics classified the paid test order as returning.
The Returning Customer revenue action is primary. The previous purchase action is secondary.
Check conversion activity in Google Ads before judging campaign performance.

best_practices: Confirm the Product Metrics workspace, Lightspeed store, and Google Ads client account before setup. Enter the Lightspeed API key and secret only in the authenticated app.
Verify consent settings and check a paid order from a known repeat customer before changing the campaign goal.
Start with one retention campaign. Keep one purchase action primary for that goal and review results before expanding the change.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API keys, passwords, tokens, or customer records into chat.
Do not make both returning-customer revenue and profit actions primary for the same goal.
Do not connect other ad channels or change unrelated campaign goals while setting up Google Ads.

faq.question: Which Lightspeed stores are supported?
faq.answer: The workflow supports Lightspeed eCom C-Series stores on the European or United States cluster.

faq.question: What counts as a returning customer?
faq.answer: Product Metrics uses the Lightspeed new-customer flag and order history. A matched customer with an earlier order counts as returning.

faq.question: Does every repeat purchase generate a conversion?
faq.answer: Each paid, matched repeat order can generate a conversion if consent allows it. Orders paid at pickup qualify only after Lightspeed marks them paid.

faq.question: When should I choose the profit action?
faq.answer: Choose profit when the campaign should optimize for margin instead of sales revenue. Activate additional costs and verify complete order costs first.

faq.question: Can the assistant switch my primary conversion goal?
faq.answer: No. You change the primary action or campaign goal in Google Ads. The assistant can guide the change and read back the conversion-action status.

faq.question: Where do I enter my Lightspeed API key and secret?
faq.answer: Enter them in the authenticated Product Metrics app. Do not share them in chat.
